cap_tip_with_a_smooth_disk.if_resolved_to_a_smooth_sphere: Untwisted Dirac index on a sphere is 0; a twist of degree d gives index d.  The 2n nodes do not select d=3 (for n=2 one has 4 nodes; for n=3 one has 6).
cap_tip_with_a_smooth_disk.obstruction: The metric on the tip circle degenerates at 2n nodes, so a C^infty cap that stays regular at those points is not given by the embedding and would have to resolve the nodes.  That resolution is an extra choice, not unique.
cap_tip_with_a_smooth_disk.regular_circle_would_match_a_hemisphere: A geodesic circle of length L matches the equator of a round sphere of radius L/(2 pi) = 1.2732395447351628; k_g = 0 matches as well, away from the nodes.

collapse_tip_to_a_point.reason: The tip circle has positive length 8.0 (for ell0=1.0); collapsing it is a different metric, not the completion.

ranked_directions.name: Frequency-n conoids, caps, and 'closed' conoid-like surfaces
ranked_directions.why: The untwisted APS index is 0 for every n.  Total curvature is always -2π.  Node count and isometry order are 2n, never 3.  No unique smooth closed surface is determined by the embedding; any genuine compact spin surface still needs a degree-3 twist to get index 3.

ranked_directions.name: C4 representations, four nodes, or twelve-bridge labelling as a finite algebra or fermion content
ranked_directions.why: C4 is abelian; its group algebra is C^4, with unitaries U(1)^4, not the SM or Pati-Salam algebra.  Counting 4 or 12 against 3×4 is numerology.

ranked_directions.name: Euler characteristic, Hopf bundle, or TS^2 as a source of the integer 3
ranked_directions.why: No connected compact surface has χ=3 (the maximum is 2).  The Hopf bundle has degree 1 (Dirac index 1).  O(2)=TS^2 has Dirac index 2; its three holomorphic sections are conformal Killing fields, not chiral generations.
